maria: Heads-up — found a scope enforcement hole. A key scoped to `embeddings:read` was able to call the chat generation route via a model alias fallback.

maria: Repro steps:
1) Create key with scope `embeddings:read` only.
2) Call POST /v1/chat/completions?model=mirage-embed-v1 (alias to mirage-3-chat under routing).
3) Response returned chat tokens instead of 403.

maria: Curl I used:
```bash
curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/completions?model=mirage-embed-v1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer EMB_KEY_XXXX" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}],"stream":false}'
```

maria: Response snippet (sanitized):
```json
{"id":"chat-123","object":"chat.completion","choices":[{"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"hi there"}}],"status":200}
```

maria: Expected 403 because token only allows embeddings, not chat.

jason: Oof. Do we have a quick log trace? Which service handled route check?

maria: Traces show request hit routing-proxy -> enforcement-middleware v1.4.2 -> model-router. enforcement-middleware queried token scopes by key_id and validated model cap flags, but it seems we treat alias->target model capabilities after route check, allowing fallback if target supports embeddings.

maria: Audit log line (from s3):
```
2026-06-05T15:12:07Z INFO request_id=abc123 key_id=emb-key-9 endpoint=/v1/chat/completions?model=mirage-embed-v1 action=allowed reason="model_alias_resolved_to:mirage-3-chat, token_scopes:embeddings:read"
```

kevin: Summary: enforcement currently checks (1) requested route capability vs token scopes OR (2) resolved model capabilities — if either matches it allows. Bug is the OR logic. Should be AND: route must be permitted AND resolved model must be allowed by token.

kevin: Proposed fix: tighten middleware to evaluate in this order:
1) resolve model alias -> canonical model id
2) compute required route permission (chat vs embed) from route + model capability
3) ensure token scopes include required permission exactly

kevin: Config diff (draft):
```json
{"runtimes":{}, "enforcement": {"require_model_resolution": true, "logic": "AND"}}
```

jason: Can we patch enforcement-middleware in a minor release and canary? What's backward compatibility impact for old tokens?

kevin: No token schema changes. Only stricter checks. Should be opt-in by default flag off for 48h then flip. Plan: deploy to canary region, enable `require_model_resolution=true` for canary, run internal smoke and -- if no regressions -- flip globally.

maria: Also recommend enabling audit-logs with KMS-wrapped key rotation so we can trace any future scope anomalies. Right now logs are plaintext in S3 for 90d, rotate with KMS and add immutability tag.

maria: KMS note: rotation for emb keys should be independent of user API key rotation. We need envelope encryption for logs.

auditbot: Audit logging flag is currently `audit.enforce_model_resolution=false` in prod. To enable audit line-level immutability: run `rbacctl audit enable --kms-key arn:aws:kms:...:alias/redwood-audit --retention 365` (requires infra approval).

jason: Who wants to own the patch and rollout? Can we pair with infra for KMS change?

kevin: I'll own the middleware patch + tests. @jason can you coordinate infra (KMS, S3 policy) and get approvals? @maria can you own the regression prompt set to run during canary?

maria: Yup, I'll produce a small eval set: variants for embeddings-only keys hitting every route, plus fuzzed model alias combos.

kevin: Tests I'll add:
- unit: alias resolution mocked -> must fail when scopes mismatch
- integration: real routing-proxy + middleware in staging with sample keys
- e2e: smoke that previously allowed path now returns 403 and an audited deny event.

deploy-bot: deployment scheduled: enforcement-middleware v1.4.3-canary -> us-west-2-canary at 2026-06-05T19:00:00Z (owner=kevin) :rocket:

jason: I'll open infra ticket for KMS and S3 immutability, link it here.

jason: infra ticket #INF-4123 created, assigned to @infra-oncall, eta 24h for approval.

maria: Also note: we should add a short-lived alert if any embeddings-scoped key has a chat route accept. Simple metric: counter in enforcement metrics labeled `scope_mismatch_allowed` should be zero. Add alert if >0 in 1m.

kevin: Good call. I'll add metric + alert to the canary dashboard.

maria: TL;DR action items:
- kevin: patch middleware + tests + deploy canary (owner)
- jason: infra KMS + audit config (owner)
- maria: regression/eval set + alert definition (owner)
- infra-oncall: approve KMS key change (action)

kevin: I'll also include a short migration doc mentioning opt-in window and rollback steps.

maria: Thanks all. Ping me when canary is up so I run evals.
